title: Hannah and the Colorful Threads
summary: The whole people bring so many gifts for the Mishkan that Moses has to announce, "Enough, there's plenty!" Little Hannah spins blue and red wool threads with the wise women, and together they help make beautiful curtains. And on Shabbat, everyone rests. A story about working together and about Shabbat.
pages:
Moses called all the people to gather.
Men, women, children and babies, they all came to listen.

"Six days you shall work," said Moses, "and the seventh day is Shabbat. A day of rest.
And now, whoever's heart wishes to, come and help build the Mishkan."

Hannah ran to the tent of the wise women.
There women sat with spinning spindles, spinning threads from wool: blue, purple and red.

"I want to do it too!" said Hannah.
Grandma Malka gave her a little spindle.
"You turn it like this, and pull slowly," she showed her.

At first Hannah's thread broke. And broke again.
But Hannah didn't give up. She turned and pulled, turned and pulled...
until she made a long, strong thread!

The wisest women did something funny: they spun threads from the goats' hair while the goats were still standing there!
"Maaa-maaa!" said the goat, and Hannah laughed and laughed.

Meanwhile, all the people kept bringing gifts: gold, silver, copper, wood, precious stones.
The women even brought their mirrors, mirrors of shiny copper.

The pile grew and grew, until the craftsmen came to Moses:
"There's more than we need!"
So Moses announced throughout the camp: "Enough! Don't bring any more. There's plenty!"

From everyone's threads, Bezalel and the craftsmen wove huge, beautiful curtains and joined them together.
Hannah searched, and found her own thread inside the curtain. She was very proud.

And on the sixth day, when the sun began to set, everyone put down their tools.
Hannah's spindle rested in the corner too.
Shabbat shalom!

On Shabbat nobody spun, sewed or built.
Hannah sat with Grandma Malka, they sang together, and ate manna that had been gathered on Friday.

Is there something you've learned to do by yourself, with patience?
And when we do something together, each with our own thread, something big and beautiful comes out.
And after working, how good it is to rest on Shabbat.
